title: Bias in Decision-Making for AI’s Ethical Dilemmas: A Comparative Study of Open-source and Closed-source Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM responses to simulated protective and harmful ethical dilemmas involving individuals with different age attributes (8, 35, 70) and measuring selection frequencies and ethical preferences.

Evaluating LLM responses to simulated protective and harmful ethical dilemmas involving individuals with different gender attributes (Masculine, Feminine, Androgynous) and measuring selection frequencies and ethical preferences.

Evaluating LLM responses to simulated protective and harmful ethical dilemmas involving individuals with different dressing attributes (Modest, Stylish, Luxury) as proxies for socioeconomic status, measuring selection frequencies and ethical preferences.

Evaluating LLM responses to simulated protective and harmful ethical dilemmas involving individuals with different race (Asian, Caucasian, African) and color (Black, White, Yellow) attributes, measuring selection frequencies and ethical preferences.

Evaluating LLM responses to simulated protective and harmful ethical dilemmas involving individuals with different look attributes (Good-looking, Standard-looking, Unpleasant-looking) and measuring selection frequencies and ethical preferences.

Evaluating LLM responses to simulated protective and harmful ethical dilemmas involving individuals with different disability attributes (Non-disabled, Disabled) and measuring selection frequencies and ethical preferences.
